summary_html: Child safely **reunified with parent or guardian**, case closed. Federal policy treats reunification as the preferred outcome once risk factors are mitigated.
authority_html:
- **Adoption and Safe Families Act (ASFA)** — establishes reunification timelines and permanency goals  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — funds reunification services and tracks permanency outcomes

primary_citations.citation_text: Montana - Title 41, Chapter 3 (Child Abuse and Neglect – mandatory reporting and protective services)

regulations_applicable.title: Department 37 - PUBLIC HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: Reversed: once the father completed his court-ordered treatment plan, the district court unconstitutionally violated his fundamental right to parent by permanently placing the child with the maternal grandmother, a nonparent, and denying him placement; the abuse and neglect proceeding should have been dismissed at that point.
key_cases.relevance: It is the Montana authority requiring reunification once the parent has done what the court ordered, and it is the strongest state-law protection against open-ended agency custody.
key_cases.quote: At that time, this proceeding should have been dismissed, leaving further consideration of the parenting relationship and parenting plan establishment in the DR matter.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed approval of a permanency plan and an award of long-term custody until the child reached 18: the Department's ICPC-based efforts to place the child with his out-of-state father were reasonable, and placement with the long-term caregiver alongside his sibling served the child's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: It is the Montana case on how far the Department must go, including through the ICPC, before reunification with a non-custodial out-of-state parent may be rejected.
key_cases.quote: Rather, “the child's health and safety are of paramount concern,” when determining what efforts are required.

key_cases.holding: Termination was affirmed: the Department made the reasonable efforts required by § 41-3-423(1) where it prepared and explained a treatment plan and offered services, even though the father never signed or returned the plan and the court approved it on the Department's motion.
key_cases.relevance: It defines how much the Department must do — more than merely suggesting services, but not herculean efforts — before reunification may be abandoned.
key_cases.quote: From our review of the record, we conclude the Department provided reasonable efforts as required by § 41-3-423(1), MCA.

key_cases.holding: A district court finding under § 41-3-403(2) that preservation or reunification services are not required because of aggravated circumstances must be supported by clear and convincing evidence, which a certified judgment for attempted rape of a child supplied here.
key_cases.relevance: It is the Montana authority defining when reunification services may lawfully be withheld, which forecloses the reunification outcome from the outset.
key_cases.quote: the district court's findings under § 41-3-403(2), MCA (1999), must be supported by clear and convincing evidence

key_cases.holding: Termination of both parents' rights was affirmed; § 41-3-423 obliges the Department to make reasonable efforts to reunify but the term cannot be defined in the abstract, each case must be evaluated on its own facts, and the statute does not require herculean efforts, so the Department's unsuccessful attempts to secure scarce, waitlisted mental-health treatment for the mother satisfied it.
key_cases.relevance: It fixes the ceiling on what the Department must do before reunification may be abandoned, holding that months-long waiting lists for the very services a psychologist recommended do not defeat a finding of reasonable efforts.
key_cases.quote: each case must be evaluated on its own facts. But clearly the statute does not require herculean efforts.
